chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Talha, from Abu Bakr ibn Isa ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, who said:

I was in the Masjid when a dead body was brought, so I wanted to pray upon it. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) came, placed his elbow on my chest, and kept pushing me until I exited the Masjid, then he said: 'O Abu Bakr! The dead bodies are not prayed upon in the Masjids.'
ai.seo_question: Where should funeral prayers be performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic preference (or prohibition, depending on the school of thought) against performing funeral prayers within the mosque, distinguishing them from the five daily congregational prayers. The physical gesture of Imam al-Hasan al-Urji (peace be upon him) pushing the narrator out serves as a practical demonstration of this ruling, reinforcing the concept that while mosques are for worship, the specific ritual of Janazah is often performed in adjacent courtyards or open spaces to maintain the sanctity and specific function of the prayer hall.
